clue.text: Select tea for a hungry dog

definitions.text: Select tea for a hungry dog

parts.words: Select tea for a hungry dog
parts.note: a fine grade of tea, which a solver can read as a Pekinese (a Peke) with nothing, O, inside it: a dog with an empty belly

explanation.surface: Someone picks out a special brew to give to a ravenous pet.
explanation.walkthrough: PEKE is short for Pekinese, a breed of dog; put O (nothing, so hungry) inside it and you have the tea's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a high-quality black tea made from young leaves, a select grade.

clue.text: Behold a revolutionary in Texan town

indicators.note: the first group of letters goes inside the word for behold, so 'in' marks the placing

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or behold
a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: An onlooker is told to look at a rebel in a town in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a city in Texas on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Quits the parade disagreeably?

parts.note: a soldier who leaves the ranks on parade does this, and so does someone who quarrels

explanation.surface: A soldier storms off the parade ground in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall out is both to leave military ranks and to quarrel, which is disagreeing.

clue.text: Come round again with a weaker concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A patient recovers consciousness after a milder potion.
explanation.definitionFit: To reawake is to wake once more, coming back to consciousness.

clue.text: State with a right to another

parts.note: Kansas is another US state, picked up from the definition

explanation.surface: A US state is described by reference to its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkansas is one of the fifty US states.

clue.text: Past grudges dug up from Wis den?

definitions.meaning: old grievances someone wants to settle
Wisden is the cricket almanac, full of historic match results, here split to look like a den in Wisconsin

explanation.surface: Ancient feuds are unearthed from a lair in Wisconsin.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisden is the annual reference book of English cricket, which records past match results; splitting it as 'Wis den' hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling old scores means avenging old wrongs; old scores are also previous cricket results recorded in an almanac.

clue.text: Not altogether a deep star explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A distant star blows up into pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are apart rather than together have been parted or split.

clue.text: Fish in a second-rate stream

parts.note: B is a second-class grade, as in B-movie
a rill is a small brook

explanation.surface: A fish is found in a poor little brook.
explanation.definitionFit: Brill is a flatfish related to the turbot.

clue.text: Show offbird Rex detailed

indicators.note: to detail here is to cut off the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to swank is to show off
Rex is Latin for king, abbreviated K

explanation.surface: A royal bird is told to stop preening.
explanation.walkthrough: SWANK loses its tail, the K for king (Rex), leaving the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan is a large long-necked water bird.

clue.text: Provision instituted in the salad days of the merry monarch

definitions.text: Provision instituted in the salad days of the merry monarch

parts.words: Provision instituted in the salad days of the merry monarch
parts.note: a statute laid down by Old King Cole, the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme, which also names a cabbage salad

explanation.surface: A historical law dates from the youthful reign of a jovial king.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is the 'merry old soul' of a nursery rhyme; his law would be Cole's law, and 'salad' hints at the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleslaw is a salad of shredded raw cabbage, which a punning reading turns into a royal statute.

clue.text: Swears it makes a natural swimmer

indicators.note: the word is made into something else, so its letters are rearranged to form the fish

explanation.surface: Cursing is supposedly what turns someone into a born swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish, so swimming comes naturally to it.

clue.text: Go round lightweight in the Mediterranean island

indicators.note: round signals turning the word for the light weight back to front

parts.note: oz, an ounce, is a small weight

explanation.surface: Someone takes a trip around a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Gozo is the second island of the Maltese archipelago in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Where a homesick Jamaican may reflect on the Thames

definitions.text: Where a homesick Jamaican may reflect on the Thames

parts.words: Where a homesick Jamaican may reflect on the Thames
parts.note: a London riverside borough sharing its name with Jamaica's capital, so a Jamaican there would think of home

explanation.surface: A Jamaican exile gazes wistfully at the river in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingston upon Thames is a borough in south-west London; Kingston is also the capital of Jamaica.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to Jamaica's capital and to a town on the Thames.

clue.text: Readily available for those most easily suited

definitions.meaning: on sale ready-made, not ordered specially
ready-made clothing fits people of standard size without tailoring

explanation.surface: Stock clothes suit people who are easy to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothes hang on store hooks and are bought without tailoring.

clue.text: Influences personal property

definitions.meaning: as a verb, brings about or affects
belongings, as in a dead person's possessions

explanation.surface: Someone's belongings sway them.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect is to bring about change, and one's effects are one's belongings.

clue.text: Encourage to grow the brinjal

parts.note: to egg on is to urge
a plant is something that grows

explanation.surface: A gardener is urged to cultivate a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: Brinjal is the South Asian name for the aubergine.
explanation.definitionFit: Brinjal and aubergine are other names for the purple vegetable called this in America.

clue.text: Made up for having abstained round the start of Eastertide

indicators.note: the word for having abstained wraps round the letter, so round marks a container

parts.note: having gone without food is having fasted

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone compensated with a big meal after a Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: After a period without food, eating lavishly compensates for it.

clue.text: Remove poor reagents

indicators.note: poor suggests the chemicals are in bad shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chemist discards substandard chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to remove them from intimacy or affection.

clue.text: Plant a girl gathers round the mountain

indicators.note: the girl's name wraps round the other piece, so this marks a container

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
ben is a Scottish word for a mountain, as in Ben Nevis

explanation.surface: A young woman collects something growing on a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a flowering garden plant, also called vervain.

clue.text: Make no move to get Satan exorcised

indicators.note: a devil driven out is thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A priest stays put rather than drive out the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to stay still and not develop or progress.

clue.text: Composer near to breakdown

indicators.note: breaking down the word means its letters fall apart and are reordered

explanation.surface: A composer is close to collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Arne was an 18th-century English composer, writer of Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was the English composer who wrote Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Blast from left to right and from right to left

indicators.text: from left to right and from right to left
indicators.note: the word spells the same in both directions, so the clue just says read it either way

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A horn sounds in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: A toot is a short blast on a horn or whistle.

clue.text: So returning Welsh girl discovers legendary poet

indicators.note: returning means the little word is turned back to front

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name

explanation.surface: A Welsh woman finds an ancient bard.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossian was the Gaelic bard whose 'translated' poems James Macpherson published in the 1760s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossian is the legendary Gaelic bard of Celtic tradition.

clue.text: Bone I break in a scrap getting up

indicators.note: the single letter breaks into the reversed phrase, so this marks an insertion
in a down clue getting up means read from bottom to top, so the phrase is reversed

parts.note: a bit is a scrap or small piece

explanation.surface: Someone fractures a leg bone in a fight while getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: A BIT reversed by 'getting up' gives TIBA, and 'break in' puts I into it.
explanation.definitionFit: The tibia is the shinbone, the larger of the two lower leg bones.

clue.text: Wizard bird

explanation.definitionFit: Merlin is King Arthur's magician and also a small falcon.

clue.text: Military cover in buff we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: in the buff means naked, with bare skin

explanation.surface: A soldier's headgear is worn by someone who is otherwise naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the buff' means naked; the tall fur caps of British Guards regiments sound like bare skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall fur cap worn by British Guards soldiers is a piece of military headgear.

clue.text: Legendary hunter she quarters

parts.note: her is the object form of she
N and E are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A woman cuts up a legendary hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: Herne the Hunter is a ghost said to haunt Windsor Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Herne the Hunter is the antlered ghost of Windsor Forest folklore.

clue.text: Mysterious breed of giant mice

indicators.note: a breed is a variety produced from stock, so the letters are bred into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange strain of huge rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic means puzzling or hard to understand.
